text: “Hear, Israel.” You have said these words every morning and every evening of your life.
Daughter! You came up for the feast too? Half of Capernaum is here. They say he will come back to the Temple today.
speaker: The fisherman from Capernaum

text: A few days later Jesus is back in the courts, answering questions from priests, Pharisees and Sadducees one after another. A scribe you know by sight has been listening at your elbow.
In the shade of a portico, two of your teachers speak quietly with a priest of the high priest’s family. When they see you, they stop.
The outer court of Herod’s Temple was open to everyone, Jews and Gentiles alike. At Passover it filled with pilgrims changing money and buying animals for sacrifice.
Scribe! You came up for the feast too? Half of Capernaum is here. They say he will come back to the Temple today.
speaker: The fisherman from Capernaum

text: The Temple tax is paid in silver of Tyre and nothing else. Your Roman coins carry Caesar’s face. I can change them for you, for a small fee.
speaker: A money changer

text: No one asks him anything after that. You find you have one question left, and you are afraid of the answer.
Coins are still rolling across the paving. What do you think?
Two doves for a mother’s purification, if she cannot afford a lamb. The priests will reject any bird with a blemish, so buy here and be sure.
speaker: A dove seller

text: In the shade of a portico, two men who eat at your uncle’s table speak quietly with a priest of the high priest’s family. When they see you, they stop.
One of the scribes came, and heard them questioning together. Knowing that he had answered them well, asked him, “Which commandment is the greatest of all?”

The scribe said to him, “Truly, teacher, you have said well that he is one, and there is none other but he, and to love him with all the heart, and with all the understanding, with all the soul, and with all the strength, and to love his neighbor as himself, is more important than all whole burnt offerings and sacrifices.”

They came to Jerusalem, and Jesus entered into the temple, and began to throw out those who sold and those who bought in the temple, and overthrew the tables of the money changers, and the seats of those who sold the doves.
The chief priests and the scribes heard it, and sought how they might destroy him. For they feared him, because all the multitude was astonished at his teaching.

Jesus answered, “The greatest is, ‘Hear, Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is one: you shall love the Lord your God with all your heart, and with all your soul, and with all your mind, and with all your strength.’ This is the first commandment. The second is like this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’ There is no other commandment greater than these.”
When Jesus saw that he answered wisely, he said to him, “You are not far from the Kingdom of God.” No one dared ask him any question after that.

He would not allow anyone to carry a container through the temple. He taught, saying to them, “Isn’t it written, ‘My house will be called a house of prayer for all the nations?’ But you have made it a den of robbers!”
Notices in Greek and Latin were set along this barrier. Two have been found. They warn that any foreigner who goes past it will have only himself to blame for the death that follows.
